what: EP-32: fixed a live update-path bug the user hit testing UPDATE_PROMPT.md -- an ad-hoc task file with no matching branch got orphan-swept and archived despite EP-29's fix. Root cause was two-layered: MIGRATIONS.md's v2.1.0 orphan-sweep bullet predated EP-29's ad-hoc-name exception and was never updated, and ai_os_version was never bumped past 2.1.1 despite EP-28/29/30/31 shipping real behavior changes, so UPDATE_PROMPT's version-gated migration walk would have skipped a corrected section anyway. Fixed the stale bullet in place, added a v2.2.0 MIGRATIONS.md section for EP-28/29/30/31 (incl. forcing commands/aliases.json's wrap key even though that file is otherwise preserve-user-customizations), bumped ai_os_version to 2.2.0 in manifest.json and README. Also fixed the same non-main-branch staleness in all 7 bridge/template files (root AGENTS.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, 5 installer templates). Separately fixed UPDATE_PROMPT.md Step 3, which unconditionally overwrote BOOT.md/kernel/rules with zero check -- any KERNEL OVERRIDE AUTHORIZED customization would be silently destroyed on update. Now searches decisions.jsonl/decisions.archive.jsonl/progress.md for KERNEL OVERRIDE entries targeting those files first, and surfaces/offers to re-merge instead of overwriting blind, using the framework's own mandatory kernel-edit logging as the signal since there's no stored baseline to diff against
why: same class of bug as the earlier README staleness catches, but this one caused an actual data-loss-adjacent failure in a live test rather than just a doc mismatch -- confirms installer/updater sync needs to happen inside the same EP that changes kernel behavior, not as a separate later pass. The kernel-overwrite gap is the same risk one level up: even correct migrations don't help if the update blindly clobbers authorized kernel customizations that were never migrations to begin with
